ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and on every material change, conduct risk-based enhanced due diligence on all UBOs, partners, directors, authorized signatories, and intermediaries. Screen against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Hong Kong Monetary Authority sanctions and counter-terrorist financing notices, and PRC/domestic anti-terrorism and financial sanctions lists. Flag all foreign, domestic, and international-organization PEPs plus their family members and close associates; apply senior-management-approved enhanced monitoring, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and transaction-pattern analysis for social-casino and in-app-purchase revenue flows. Any positive hit or unexplained suspicion requires immediate review and a Suspicious Transaction Report to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) of Hong Kong; no tipping off is permitted; records must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR – e-Registry / Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) name search and incorporation application portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Companies Registry accepts an English name in Latin script and/or a Chinese name in Traditional Chinese characters; simplified Chinese characters are not accepted in the Chinese name field. The English and Chinese names need not be phonetically identical, but must not be misleading or create confusion with existing names. Four-tier review applies: (1) mandatory statutory suffix for limited companies; (2) script and transliteration compliance; (3) uniqueness and absence of misleading similarity; and (4) prohibited and sensitive-token screening.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Hong Kong Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) as amended, including section 4 (constitution and registration of limited partnerships), section 7 (registration of limited partnership), section 8 (registered office and statement filed), and section 35 (regulatory powers); Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) as applied to limited partnerships; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 5 (obligation to register business); and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) to the extent applicable to the financial operations of the partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Limited Partnerships Registry; and the Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR for business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37), accompanied by the executed Limited Partnership Agreement; and the prescribed Business Registration application form under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under Hong Kong law. The Limited Partnership Ordinance does not prescribe any minimum paid-up capital, and no blocked escrow account or statutory capital deposit is required. The amount, currency, and drawdown schedule of capital commitments are purely contractual and must be recorded in the Limited Partnership Agreement. For banking and AML/KYC purposes, the partners may nevertheless agree to fund an initial operating deposit at a licensed financial institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [GENERAL PARTNER] LIMITED AS CORPORATE GENERAL PARTNER AND OF THE LIMITED PARTNERS OF CN FIP (HK) L.P.

WHEREAS:

(A) The Partnership is to be constituted as a limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong, with the name CN FIP (HK) L.P., using a foreign-invested limited partner base and a pass-through tax classification permissible in Hong Kong.

(B) The corporate general partner is a private limited company validly incorporated in Hong Kong, and its board of directors has been duly convened with the requisite quorum and notice.

(C) The Partnership will carry on the business of publishing simulated social casino and virtual slots software under ISIC 5820, distributed through online app stores and digital payment rails such as Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED by the unanimous vote of all directors of the corporate general partner and with the unanimous written consent of the limited partners as follows:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTIONS. Each partner subscribes to the capital contributions set forth in the Limited Partnership Agreement, which is hereby approved and adopted. Drawdowns of committed capital shall be made only upon at least five business days written notice to each partner and shall be credited to the capital account of each contributing partner in the statutory books maintained at the Registered Office. No partner shall be required to contribute beyond the committed amount except by a future written resolution approved by all partners.

2. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Partnership be and is hereby fixed at [full address in Hong Kong]. The corporate general partner is authorized and directed to file Form LP1 and all subsequent notices of change of registered office with the Companies Registry, and to keep the statutory registers, minutes, and records at that address.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Partnership shall open and maintain bank accounts with [authorized institution]. [Name] and [Name] are appointed as authorized signatories, and any two signatories jointly, one of whom must be a director of the corporate general partner, may sign cheques, wire transfer instructions, internet banking mandates, deposit account forms, and all related instruments. The bank is authorized to rely on a certified copy of this resolution and on any certificate signed by the Compliance Officer confirming the current signatory list and account mandate.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS AND AUTHORIZED REPRESENTATIVES. [Name] is appointed as the authorized representative before the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office. [Name] is appointed as Compliance Officer and principal AML/CTF officer. [Name] is appointed as secretary of the corporate general partner. Each such officer is empowered to execute statutory declarations, annual returns, tax filings, service of process acceptances, and banking forms on behalf of the Partnership.

5. BUSINESS REGISTRATION AND TAX FILING. The authorized representative shall apply for the Business Registration Certificate within the statutory period and shall ensure that all profits tax filings are made when due. The corporate general partner shall obtain tax advice before asserting any offshore claim or claiming any exclusion from Hong Kong source taxation.

6. RATIFICATION. All acts, filings, payments, and agreements undertaken by the incorporators, counsel, and prospective officers in connection with the formation of the Partnership are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted in all respects.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall continue until revoked by a later resolution of the corporate general partner with the consent of the limited partners. Certified copies shall be provided to the bank, the Companies Registry, the Inland Revenue Department, and any other authority upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and partnership governance design
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Hong Kong SAR - Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) and Central Registration Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a live search through the Companies Registry's Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) for the intended partnership name. The name must end with the suffix 'L.P.' and must not be identical to an existing Hong Kong company, limited partnership, or foreign registered non-Hong Kong company. Confirm that the name contains no prohibited term that would suggest government patronage or require separate regulatory consent. Generate and preserve a name search report for the client file. Before proceeding, verify the identity, nationality, residential or business address, and proposed capital commitment of each general and limited partner. If the corporate general partner is not yet incorporated, incorporate it as a Hong Kong private limited company and obtain its certificate of incorporation before the limited partnership registration is submitted.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and intended place of business address
ICRIS name search report
Passport or national identity document of each prospective partner
Proof of residential or business address for each partner
Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution if the general partner is a corporate entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry rejects or queries the proposed name, submit two alternative names in order of preference. If the query relates to a partner's identity or authorization, provide legalized or notarized identity documents and a signed power of attorney. The Companies Registry typically allows a cure period of 14 days from the date of the requisition letter; respond within that period with corrected information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and filing of Form LP1 and Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Limited Partnerships Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the name search is cleared, finalize and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement, which must specify the capital commitments, profit and loss sharing percentages, management authority of the general partner, duration, dissolution triggers, and restrictions on limited partner participation in management. Complete Form LP1 in the prescribed form and have it signed by the general partner. If the general partner is a corporation, attach a certified copy of its certificate of incorporation, the corporate board resolution approving the partnership, and a notarized certificate as to the directors and registered office of the corporate general partner. Submit the entire package to the Companies Registry by post, in person, or through the electronic filing window, and pay the prescribed registration fee. Upon successful verification, the Registrar will issue the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 signed by the general partner or its authorized representative
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Certified copy of the corporate general partner's certificate of incorporation and board resolution
Notarized passport copies and address proofs of all partners
Registered office address consent from the landlord or service provider
Original or certified copy of the Name Search acceptance letter, if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or suspends the application, file a written response with corrected documents within 14 days. If the issue involves improper notarization, obtain a fresh certificate from a Hong Kong notary public. If the capital contribution description is unclear, file an amended Form LP1 reflecting the exact committed amounts and payment dates. If fees were underpaid, settle the shortfall before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the authorized representative must apply to the Business Registration Office within one month of the commencement of business. Complete the prescribed business registration application form, declare the principal place of business in Hong Kong, and attach a copy of the limited partnership certificate, the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, and identification documents for all partners. Pay the current business registration fee and levy. The Business Registration Office will issue the Business Registration Certificate bearing the business registration number, the name of the partnership, the nature of business, and the validity period. Display the certificate in a conspicuous place at the registered office, retain a duplicate copy for bank onboarding, and use the business registration number in all tax correspondence and compliance filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership issued by the Companies Registry
Completed Business Registration application form as prescribed by the Inland Revenue Department
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Identification and address proof for each partner
Hong Kong registered office address proof
Business registration fee and levy payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office rejects the application or issues an inquiry, provide the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, a letter of explanation signed by the general partner, and any missing address or identity proof. If a late filing penalty has been imposed, submit a written mitigation request with a reasonable excuse supported by documentary evidence. The Commissioner has discretion to reduce or remit penalties in meritorious cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account onboarding, statutory records, and corporate governance implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank authorized by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Board of the Corporate General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting of the corporate general partner and obtain the partner consents required to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution contained in this dossier. Execute the bank account opening forms and present the formation certificate, business registration certificate, partnership agreement, board resolution, identity documents, source of funds, and beneficial ownership declaration to the selected bank. Maintain at the registered office the statutory register of partners, a copy of the Limited Partnership Agreement, minutes of resolutions, accounting records, and all AML/KYC documents. Ensure that any future change of general partner, capital contribution, registered office, or partnership name is filed with the Companies Registry within the statutory filing window. The Compliance Officer shall also retain the Apple App Store and Google Play developer agreements, privacy policy, terms of service, and any platform policy confirmations necessary for lawful distribution of the simulated social casino software.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the First Board Resolution including banking authorization and officer appointments
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Certificate of incorporation and board resolution of the corporate general partner
AML/KYC declaration with source of funds and beneficial ownership chart
Apple App Store and Google Play developer agreements or platform approval documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the account application, request a written adverse decision, supplement the beneficial ownership and source of funds explanation, and approach another licensed bank through a professional introducer. If the Companies Registry questions the statutory records, file the required amendment form with a supporting resolution within 14 days. If a data protection or AML concern is raised, the Compliance Officer shall remediate the policy and internal controls before resubmission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Pure Digital Software Publishing (ISIC 5820) with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing site in Hong Kong.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing or physical operating license is required. The distribution of simulated social casino and virtual slots games through Apple App Store and Google Play is subject to the respective platform policies and developer agreements. No gambling license under the Hong Kong Gambling Ordinance (Cap. 148) is required because the game content does not involve real-money wagering, betting, or cash redemption.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operation has zero point-source wastewater, VOC, toxic air emissions, or hazardous waste generation. Cloud-hosted digital services are outside the schedules of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499). Only ordinary office and data-center electrical consumption and electronic waste disposal obligations may apply, and those are not EIA-triggering activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical premises require a Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety certificate. If the Partnership later leases an office, the landlord must ensure compliance with the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) and the Fire Safety (Commercial Premises) Ordinance (Cap. 502), and the Partnership must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) for office workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), accessible via the 'National Electronic Tax Bureau' (eTax portal) at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn, with local counterpart administration at the municipal district tax service hall within the registered address jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) established under the PRC Partnership Enterprise Law and the Foreign Investment Law, the primary tax identifier is the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), automatically obtained upon completion of business registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Thereafter, the FIP must complete taxpayer registration with the competent tax authority through the 'New Electronic Tax Bureau' by submitting the partnership registration certificate, articles of partnership, a copy of the foreign investor's passport or company registration certificate, proof of the registered address (e.g., lease agreement and property ownership certificate), and the bank account opening permit or basic deposit account information. The tax authority will issue an electronic tax registration form and confirm the tax classification. For foreign non-resident partners or foreign enterprises without a permanent establishment in China that have Chinese-source income, a Non-Resident Taxpayer Identification Number (NTN) must be applied for through the withholding agent using the Tax Withholding Filing Form for Contracts (Contract Filing for Withholding Tax), with supporting documentation of the contract and the non-resident entity's foreign registration certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide a check-the-box election under domestic law for partnership taxation. The FIP is pass-through for enterprise income tax purposes: profit is allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level (corporate enterprise income tax at 25% or individual income tax five-level progressive rates). No hybrid mismatch election is available under the current PRC administrative rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual assessable turnover for compulsory general taxpayer registration; foreign-invested partnership is subject to small-scale taxpayer registration from initiation if below this threshold, and a non-resident digital supplier triggers VAT registration when cumulative assessable digital services sales to Chinese customers exceed RMB 500,000 in any rolling 12-month period. All enterprises, including FIPs, must complete tax registration and obtain a taxpayer identification number at entity formation regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the 'Golden Tax Phase IV' digital infrastructure with mandatory 'Full Digital Electronic Invoice' (Full Digital E-Invoice / Shu Dian Piao) issuance and real-time transmission of invoice data to the STA's central electronic tax database upon issuance. The issuance system uses a unique nationwide invoice number, anti-fraud cryptographic stamping, and automated conformance checking of invoice limits against the taxpayer's prior declaration and tax credit rating. The FIP must apply for electronic invoice quotas and issuance authorizations through the eTax platform, and all sales must be recorded using the prescribed Goods and Services tax classification codes. No alternative paper invoice is permitted unless obtained from the tax authority in extraordinary cases. The platform payment rails (Apple IAP and Google Play Billing) must generate transactional records reconciling with invoice issuance for VAT filing obligations; if the FIP uses the foreign multinational platform as the collection agent, the contractual arrangement and platform reports must evidence the underlying trade for VAT and foreign exchange compliance.

The digital invoice platform requires prior system integration or manual issuance interface setup; real-time synchronization to the tax authority is mandatory before declaring output VAT; the anti-fraud digital stamp is automatically generated by the national system and cannot be omitted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for exported software publishing and digital services under STA Notice 2016 No. 36 and related implementing circulars, provided the service is supplied to an overseas recipient (outside mainland China), the actual consumption takes place wholly offshore, the contractual payment is received in foreign exchange from outside China, and the exporter is a general VAT taxpayer. Cross-border supply of simulated casino and social slots game publishing to Hong Kong SAR users can qualify as an offshore software-and-information-technology service only where the FIP has obtained approval for the relevant tax-exempt or zero-rated cross-border service filing and the destination of the digital service is substantiated as Hong Kong SAR. The FIP must complete the cross-border service exemption or zero-rating filing with the competent tax authority using the prescribed registration platform. Digital gaming services supplied through app store platforms may be zero-rated where the contractual service recipient is the overseas app store operator or a Hong Kong consumer, and where the payment chain and platform statements show foreign currency remittance minus platform commission.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) applicable to physical media containing software or, for pure digital services, the cross-border service filing record and project undertaking from the eTax platform
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill only for physical exports, or platform electronic service performance report for digital exports

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by the receiving bank or the bank's foreign exchange settlement record (Bank International Settlement Certificate) showing foreign currency repatriation from overseas
International service contract or end-user license agreement identifying the foreign recipient and the offshore consumption jurisdiction
Payment processor settlement records from Apple IAP / Google Play Billing showing the gross receipts, commission deduction, net remittance, and country-level breakdown of sales to Hong Kong users
Digital service completion certificate or performance evidence showing the server access and gameplay occurred outside mainland China
Business registration certificate of the Hong Kong counterparty (if the technology intermediary is in Hong Kong) or HK address and IP evidence for direct consumer sales
VAT invoice issued in accordance with the electronic invoicing system marked 'Export Sales' or 'Zero-Rated Cross-Border Service'
Software copyright certificate or software product certificate evidencing that the game software authenticity and ownership belong to the FIP
Foreign exchange receiving bank statement reconciling the exact export consideration with the invoice and platform settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: For claimed export zero-rating or VAT exemption, the tax authority may conduct a post-refund audit requesting the entire documentation bundle. Failure to produce FIRC or equivalent foreign exchange receipt within 180 days from the date of export, or within the extended time approved, triggers reversal of the zero-rating, output VAT clawback with statutory late-payment interest at 0.05% per day, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax underpaid if fraud or negligence is established. Fraudulent zero-rating declarations may be prosecuted as tax evasion under the PRC Criminal Law Article 204, with imprisonment and fines; an enterprise in violation may be deregistered as a general taxpayer or barred from future VAT zero-rating and export refund facilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for Hong Kong bank and clearing channels
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Hong Kong operates a freely convertible currency regime with no exchange controls and no approval requirement for current or capital account remittances; the HKD is anchored through the Linked Exchange Rate system at between 7.75 and 7.85 per US dollar and multi-currency accounts are freely allowed. By contrast, mainland China applies a rigorous dual-tier system: current account convertibility is permitted after documentary verification, while capital account conversion, including equity injections into a Foreign-Invested Partnership, requires SAFE registration, a capital verification report by a certified public accountant, and a designated foreign exchange capital account that restricts the use of funds to the registered business purpose. Profit distribution and partnership remittances from a mainland FIP to an HK partner must be supported by audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and a written application through the bank for SAFE-affirmed repatriation. Non-financial RMB cannot be freely delivered from onshore China to Hong Kong; offshore CNH can be accumulated or hedged through the HK market. The practical convertibility position is therefore fully free in HKSAR, fee-based and document-controlled in mainland China, and non-deliverable for pure RMB capital arbitrage across the border.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mainland China: export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated and verified through the SAFE trade-in-goods monitoring system, generally within 90 days from the date of export or the contractual settlement period; there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio into RMB, but proceeds must be deposited in a designated foreign exchange settlement account or converted to RMB based on authentic trade background. Hong Kong: no surrender requirement, no statutory conversion ratio, and no timeline for retention of export or sales proceeds in HKD or foreign currency.

Capital Escrow Account for SAFE-linked FDI flows; RMB and CNH clearing account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs incorporated outside Hong Kong and outside mainland China are not viable as primary treasury rails because they lack a SAFE licence for onshore FX and RMB settlement and generally do not hold a Hong Kong deposit-taking licence under the Banking Ordinance; using them to hold client funds would be unlawful in a regulated context. HKMA-authorized virtual banks such as ZA Bank, Mox Bank and Livi Bank may be used as secondary operating accounts, but they are not classified as offshore EMIs and still require the same corporate KYB plus sector review. For a medium-risk gaming-adjacent FIP, virtual banks may decline the relationship if the social casino classification is ambiguous; an MSO licence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance would be required for any non-bank remittance business. The recommended structure is therefore a primary Tier-1 commercial bank account and, at most, one licensed virtual bank for contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the mainland registered FIP, the legal representative and at least one authorised signatory must appear physically at a Chinese bank branch, with original partnership seal and official chop, because no statutory remote online opening exists for a foreign-invested partnership. For the Hong Kong treasury entity, HKMA guidance allows electronic KYC and video interviews, but the banking risk rating for a gaming-linked partnership typically triggers an in-branch interview for all directors, named partners and ultimate beneficial owners; a remote consular proxy opening is not a statutory right, although a notarized and apostilled power of attorney plus a local professional introducer can be used if the designated bank policy permits it. Banks will also require certified true copies of passports, proof of residential addresses, UBO declarations and board/partner resolutions before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership veil and multi-tier beneficial ownership structure creates an opaque UBO chain, especially where limited partners are passive offshore vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified register of partners; constitutional documents of every intermediate vehicle; UBO declaration for each partner holding 10% or more; executed partnership agreement; notarized passports and proof of residential address; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters; bank reference letters from current relationship banks; independent corporate structure chart; and power of attorney with notarial certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medium-risk enhanced sector red flag: virtual slots or simulated casino operations may be misinterpreted as illegal gambling or used to layer illicit proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion confirming non-money, non-wager, no-cash-out social casino mechanics; game design documentation demonstrating virtual-only tokens and terminal redemption; enforceable terms of use prohibiting secondary-market trading; Apple Developer and Google Play console agreements; app-store submission showing age/content compliance; independent audit report of payout mechanics; geo-blocking controls for regulated gambling jurisdictions; and player AML policy with no fiat redemption features.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border merchant acquiring and consumer payment exposure through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing can display high refund volatility, aggregated funds flow, and possible sanctions or travel-rule deficiencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple and Google payment processing agreements; settlement reconciliation statements for the last 12 months; sanctions and PEP screening policies covering UN, EU, OFAC, HKSAR and PRC designations; geo-IP block logs and device fingerprinting reports; transaction monitoring rules and case reports; refund/chargeback policy; ISO 27001 certificate; and a written AML/CFT policy signed by the designated compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from the HK treasury hub into the mainland FIP may fail SAFE or capital-verification scrutiny if the source of funds and registration chain are not evidenced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE foreign-exchange registration certificate; NDRC and MOFCOM outbound investment approvals as applicable; capital verification report from a certified public accountant; bank statements of the HK investing entity for 12 months; board and partner resolutions approving the capital contribution; audited financial statements of the investors; tax clearance certificates; and the executed loan-equity contribution agreement referencing the registered capital account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Group payments should be routed as SWIFT MT103 from an HK Tier-1 bank to the mainland FIP's SAFE-designated foreign exchange capital account, with the remittance purpose coded as equity contribution to a foreign-invested partnership and the SAFE registration number stated in the field-72 narrative. The onshore receiving bank will perform capital verification, compare the contribution to the registered partnership capital schedule, and allow RMB settlement only after tax and SAFE documentation checks. For capital movements initiated inside Hong Kong, no HKMA approval is required; the bank will apply CDD and request the investment agreement, source-of-funds questionnaire and declaration of commercial rationale. HKD/USD conversions can be executed at the spot rate, while any onshore RMB requirement should be sourced through CNH conversion and settled through CNAPS once SAFE approval to use the funds is granted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for operational disbursements, royalties, intercompany charges, and non-trade foreign payments; use an irrevocable at-sight Commercial Letter of Credit for goods-based trade settlements with a confirming HK bank where supplier risk exists; and use Documentary Collections (documents against payment or documents against acceptance) for lower-value repetitive trade flows. For the digital gaming treasury, Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds should be received by the HK entity through an acquiring bank or an MSO-licensed payment processor that settles via SWIFT/CHATS to the primary currency account, after which reconciliation can be made against app-store net revenue reports. Outbound vendor compensations and contractor payments should be made by MT103 or through the bank's hosted file payment engine, with all supporting trade and service contracts retained for audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts for HKD/USD, USD/CNH and HKD/CNH under an ISDA Master Agreement with a licensed HKMA bank, with maximum tenor of 12 months and strict underlying exposure mapping.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY and HKD/CNY to hedge onshore RMB exposure when physical delivery of CNY is unavailable or legally restricted.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to convert HKD or USD floating-rate liabilities into RMB-linked cash flows, provided they hedge the principal and interest of an existing or committed debt facility.
Short-dated FX swap and rollover structures for liquidity management, subject to the bank's credit limits, mark-to-market collateral, and no speculative or naked short positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Registration Certificate Renewal for the Foreign-Invested Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong SAR, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date printed on the current Business Registration Certificate; the certificate is valid for one year and the renewal is anniversary-based with no statutory grace period. Application may be made one month before the anniversary, but renewal must be completed by the expiry date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal exposes the partnership, its general partners and any responsible licensed agent to a maximum fine of HKD 5,000 and imprisonment for up to 6 months under the Business Registration Ordinance; the Inland Revenue Department may also impose a statutory late-renewal penalty of up to HKD 3,000, and prolonged non-payment/non-renewal may result in the Business Registration being struck off on the ground that the business has ceased to operate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong SAR, Profits Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the date of issue of Form BIR52; where the partnership's annual accounting period ends on 31 December, IRD customarily grants an e-filing extension to 15 August of the following year; for accounting periods ending 1 January to 31 March, the customary e-filing extension is to 15 November of the same year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse may trigger an estimated assessment, a fine of up to HKD 10,000, and additional tax of up to 3 times the amount of undercharged tax under section 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance; continuing default may lead to prosecution, distraint over partnership assets, and insolvency/bankruptcy proceedings against the general partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56A and BIR56B) where the partnership has employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong SAR, Employer's Return Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the issue date printed on the Employer's Return; the return is normally issued in April each year for remuneration paid during the preceding year of assessment, and the exact due date shown on the form must be observed, with a standard 14-day extension for e-filing where so stated by IRD.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing, incorrect disclosure or omission of employee remuneration can result in a fine of up to HKD 10,000 per offence and a daily default penalty under the Inland Revenue Ordinance; intentional misstatement may additionally expose the partnership and its partners to enhanced penalties of up to 3 times the tax that would otherwise have been chargeable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Compliance Confirmation and Change-of-Particulars Readiness Declaration for the partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR (on file for change-of-particulars forms; no separate annual partnership return is required under the Companies Ordinance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: There is no anniversary-based annual return for an unincorporated partnership; however, any change in the identity or profit-sharing percentage of a general or limited partner, change of registered address, or alteration to the registered capital/contribution must be lodged with the Companies Registry within 7 days after the change, and the Business Registration Office must be notified within 30 days of any material change. The annual secretarial calendar should therefore be locked to the partnership's anniversary date to refresh the UBO records and verify that all prior changes have been filed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to lodge a required change-of-particulars statement may render the responsible general partner liable to a fine of up to HKD 5,000 and a continuing daily default fine; persistent non-compliance or repeated failure to maintain accurate partner and beneficial-owner records may cause the licensed corporate service provider to resign, and the Companies Registry may initiate deregistration of the limited partnership arm if the partnership appears inactive or ceased operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), an incorporated Hong Kong company is required to appoint a certified public accountant to audit its financial statements regardless of size, unless the dormant-company exemption applies; however, this Foreign-Invested Partnership is an unincorporated partnership and therefore no statutory size-based audit threshold (balance-sheet total, turnover or headcount) automatically applies under Hong Kong law. A mandatory independent certified CPA audit will, however, arise where any one of the following conditions is satisfied: (a) the partnership is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund under Cap. 637 and its limited partnership agreement or regulatory offering requires annual audited accounts; (b) the partnership is licensed as, or registered as, a money service operator, virtual asset service provider, payment institution, or any regulated financial/banking entity, in which case audit is a licensing/AML condition; (c) any commercial agreement with Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, an acquiring bank, a payment gateway, or a gaming-service counterparty imposes an audit covenant, typically where annual gross processed receipts exceed HKD 10,000,000 or committed facilities exceed HKD 20,000,000; (d) the partnership is required by a PRC parent company's Chinese statutory audit to be consolidated, in which case PRC accounting-law thresholds at the parent level trigger the audit; or (e) any non-Hong Kong regulator in a target distribution market requires a licensed independent audit as a condition of lawful cross-border software publishing. There are no legal Hong Kong balance-sheet/turnover/headcount exemptions applicable to this partnership because the default audit status is 'not statutorily required'; where audit is undertaken, it must be performed by a Hong Kong Certified Public Accountant holding a valid Practice Certificate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are converged with IFRS; HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) may be used only if the partnership has no public accountability and is not required by regulators or its constitutive documents to apply full HKFRS/IFRS. Where the partnership is consolidated into a Mainland China parent, the underlying accounting records should be adjusted to PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC GAAP) for the parent's consolidation, while standalone Hong Kong statutory records may continue under HKFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foreign-Invested Partnership is not a Hong Kong company and therefore does not file the Companies Registry Significant Controllers Register annual confirmation. Nonetheless, under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Ordinance (Cap. 615) and the licensing conditions applicable to the corporate secretarial partner, the partnership must at all times maintain a current beneficial-ownership register at the Hong Kong registered office. Annual confirmation must be completed no later than 30 days after the partnership's financial year-end, and any change in beneficial ownership or transfer of partnership interest must be reported to the compliance officer and UBO register within 7 days of actual knowledge, with the Companies Registry change-of-partner statement filed within 7 days and the Business Registration Office updated within 30 days. The licensed agent must issue a written annual UBO and partnership-particulars reconciliation certificate to the general partners and retain it for at least 7 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners showing names, addresses, contributions and powers
Register of Limited Partners showing capital contributions, profit-share percentages and distribution entitlements
Register of Charges/Mortgages and any securities or liens over partnership assets
Register of Beneficial Owners and Ultimate Beneficial Ownership map maintained under Cap. 615
Partnership Resolution Book / Minute Book of Partnership and Management Committee meetings
Books of Account, bank statements, payment-gateway settlement records and supporting vouchers covering the last 7 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 1,300 per annum for a Hong Kong registered office, licensed corporate service provider, registered agent, and maintenance of the statutory registers and UBO file
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 10,000 per annum for an independent certified CPA audit of a social-casino software and virtual-slots publishing partnership with moderate transaction volumes; fees increase to USD 12,000 - USD 25,000 if gaming-licence attestations, multi-jurisdictional transfer pricing, or PRC GAAP consolidation support are required
